trickyParts: A `rank` present with neither neighbour is not a no-op: the server falls through to lastProjectRank and ranks the issue last in its project (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/issue_rank.go:51-53), which is how the web board's move-to-the-end works. The executor's spread idiom would have serialised a two-undefined object as "rank":{}, so every ordinary `dispatch issue-update --status …` would have dropped its issue to the bottom of the board. The body carries a rank key only when at least one argument is a string, locked by the recorded-fetch test and re-proven live.

The executor block already binds locals named `before` (the issue read before the PATCH) and `after` (the PATCH's answer), both used throughout the printed changes; the new arguments are read as rankBefore and rankAfter.

An empty value (`--before ''`) is counted as a field by the tool on purpose, so the call reaches the server and gets the server's own `rank neighbor must name another issue` rather than a tool-level refusal. It is not a clear, unlike `--parent ''` and `--repo ''`.
The contracts test's `{ issue, rank: "a0" }` refusal is kept as the guard, under strict: true, that the tool takes two flat arguments and no nested rank object.

packages/claude-envoy's committed dist/ and legion/ are generated: the tool strings and the controller skill live there too, and `bun run build` from packages/claude-envoy is the only way to update them. Its dist-fresh test compares against a build made with that package as the working directory (as CI runs it), so running it from the repository root reports a false mismatch in the bundle's module paths.
